title: Player.CharacterAdded
summary: Fires every time a player's character (re)spawns — including the first spawn. The right place for per-spawn logic: connecting Died, equipping items, applying buffs.

details.heading: Fresh model every time
details.body: Each spawn is a NEW Model with a NEW Humanoid. Connections made on the old character do not carry over — re-wire everything per spawn.

explanation.whatItIs: The respawn bell. Characters die and are rebuilt constantly; this event marks each fresh body.
explanation.whyItExists: Per-spawn setup is unavoidable (death hooks, loadouts); per-PLAYER setup isn't enough because bodies keep changing.
whenToUse: Giving spawn equipment or applying modifiers
whenNotToUse: Once-per-session setup — that belongs in PlayerAdded
tips: Nested pattern: PlayerAdded → CharacterAdded → Died covers the whole lifecycle
Also check `player.Character` right after connecting — a character may already exist
Use WaitForChild inside for Humanoid if you need it immediately
commonMistakes: Connecting Died once in PlayerAdded — after the first death there's no hook on the new humanoid
Holding old character references across respawns
Assuming CharacterAdded fires before the character is fully loaded — WaitForChild the parts you need

examples.title: Per-spawn death hook
examples.code:
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
        local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
        humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
            print(player.Name .. " died — respawn incoming")
        end)

        -- spawn loadout:
        -- giveTool(player, "StarterSword")
    end)

    -- Cover the already-spawned case:
    if player.Character then
        -- (same setup; in real code extract to a function)
    end
end)
